cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Hello and welcome to the film making podcast. In this week's episode, Claire Lemarre talks to us about how to become a makeup artist. Claire's been working as a makeup artist in the film industry for over 20 years and has lots of useful advice about how to get started.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Thanks Ian. Well, before you can become a makeup artist on films you have to spend about 2 years working as a makeup trainee.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: A good place to get your first job would be on a low budget short film.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Of course, this means that you'll be working for free.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: But it's often worth it for the experience.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Make sure your transport costs are covered – and remember, there's very unlikely to be any catering provided, so bring plenty of food.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: If you're lucky, you might start out on a big budget film where you'll get the most useful experience.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: On productions like this, makeup and hair styling are separate departments – so you won't need to bring your curling tongs!

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: But you're likely to get the opportunity to work with a range of age groups, as well as different ethnicities.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Doing makeup for special effects is highly specialised, so don't expect to be offered any practical experience in that.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: One problem with working in the makeup department is that it's a high-pressure environment.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: There are very few times when you'll be bored or have nothing to do.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: It can be stressful but you'll see that the top makeup artists are very professional – even when they're having to work with directors who are impatient, or unhappy with the makeup artist's work.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Follow your supervisor's lead and try to remain calm at all times.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: I've worked with many very famous actors over the years.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: At first, I found it overwhelming and could hardly speak, I was so in awe.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: That's preferable, by the way, to becoming too excited and asking for selfies.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Now meeting the talent is just a normal part of the job and to be honest most actors don't look that special without all the makeup!

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Every makeup trainee will need a makeup kit, which they'll be expected to have with them at all times.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Just the essentials will do for the kinds of tasks you'll be given – it won't be anything complicated.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: It's worth looking at what the other makeup artists have in their kits – but whatever you do, don't borrow anything without asking first.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: It's very important to build your portfolio.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: You should take photos of all the work you do and ideally show the different stages of makeup application if you can.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: But remember you'll need to get approval from the makeup designer in charge of the department.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: As you'll be sending your portfolio digitally, you won't need to get photos printed.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: So what does a makeup trainee actually do? You need to think about whether you're the right kind of person to do the job and whether you'd enjoy it. So, to give you some idea, here are some of the things you might be required to do.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: You may be asked to help prep an actor ready for makeup.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Some actors will arrive having already cleansed and moisturized their skin.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: But sometimes you'll need to step in and get this done without wasting any time, otherwise the makeup artist will get behind schedule.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Trainees play a useful role in continuity.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: It will be your responsibility to take photos, log them digitally and print out a hard copy to put in each actor's file.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: This information needs to be kept in good order as a reshoot can mean replicating makeup months later.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: General duties mean doing anything from getting the teas and coffees to putting on a wash.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Having a positive attitude and being willing to do whatever is asked of you will help you get your next film job.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: You won't be asked to apply makeup to any of the principal cast, only the extras.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: If there are dozens of extras involved you'll need to keep up a swift pace and not spend too long on each person.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: It takes quite a lot of confidence to be able to do this well.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: OK now about terms and conditions....
